subject: Transient slab / safetyband SLA addendum — Valence Bio Dedicated
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Elena Torres <elena@valencebio.com>, Markus Eriksen <markus@valencebio.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Transient slab / safetyband SLA addendum — Valence Bio Dedicated

Hi Elena / Markus —

Thanks again for the deep conversation yesterday. Per request from your infra and procurement teams, attaching a first-pass SLA addendum that defines how Redwood will support transient (burst) capacity on your Dedicated GPU pool while preserving your latency SLO and predictable billing.

High-level summary (see attached SLA-addendum-draft-v1.pdf and transient_capacity_matrix.xlsx):
- Safetyband (headroom): Redwood will reserve a configurable safetyband for Valence Bio equivalent to 20% of committed vGPU capacity during weekdays 08:00–20:00 PST, with a 10% baseline for off-hours. This is configurable in your Dedicated plan.
- Shoulder reserve: For predictable bursts (e.g., model retrains, scheduled batch-inference windows), we propose a shoulder reserve pool you can commit to monthly with discounted overage pricing.
- Autoscale policy: Continuous multi-granularity scaling (1–4 GPU increments) with a 3-minute scale-up cooldown and a 12-minute cooldown on scale-down to protect KV-cache warmup. Canary ramp for major >16 GPU ramps.
- Preemptible fallback: If safetyband exhausted, requests will fall back to preemptible instances or a smaller quantized model variant; tails will be instrumented in our console.
- Billing: Burst usage billed by-minute per-GPU with capped daily overage based on shoulder-reserve level. Pricing table attached.

Open questions for your team:
1) Typical burst frequency (daily peaks per week/month)?
2) Tail latency tolerance (95th/99th percentiles) during burst events?
3) Any blackout windows where preemptible fallback is unacceptable?

Action items proposed:
- Valence to confirm burst cadence + acceptable tail latency.
- Redwood to produce a runbook for cache-warmup and preloading KV for your top 10 endpoints.
- Procurement to review pricing CSV and sign SLA addendum if acceptable.

Attaching the two files for reference: transient_capacity_matrix.xlsx, SLA-addendum-draft-v1.pdf.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call to walk through the canary/scaling graphs.

– Rishi
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Dr. Elena Torres <elena@valencebio.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Markus Eriksen <markus@valencebio.com>, Procurements Team <procure@valencebio.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transient slab / safetyband SLA addendum — Valence Bio Dedicated

Rishi —

Thank you — this looks like a good starting point. A few clarifications from our side:

- Burst cadence: for our discovery workloads we see heavy bursts roughly 2–3× per weekday (peak windows ~09:00–11:00 and 14:00–16:00 PT), and an irregular long-burst weekly job (2–4 hours) for model re-training on Fridays.
- Tail tolerance: we need 95th <= 350ms for our interactive endpoints; 99th can be up to 900ms for non-interactive batch endpoints.
- Blackout windows: none absolutely required today but we'd like to avoid preemptible fallbacks for the interactive endpoints during peak windows if possible.

Questions: the 3-minute scale-up cooldown — is that fast enough to meet the 95th requirement during sudden spikes? Also, the shoulder-reserve pricing CSV shows an hourly min commitment; can that be converted to a weekly commit for our budgeting?

Can we schedule a 30-min technical alignment next week? Markus will join; I'll invite procurement.

— Elena
Director, Platform Engineering
Valence Bio
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Elena Torres <elena@valencebio.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transient slab / safetyband SLA addendum — Valence Bio Dedicated

Thanks for the rapid reply, Elena —

Quick technical notes to help the call:
- 3-minute scale-up cooldown is a conservative default to avoid oscillation. For interactive endpoints where 95th=350ms is required, we can shorten the aggressive fast-path scale-up to 45–90 seconds using predictive pre-warming when a burst signal is detected (traffic forecast + queue depth + token-rate heuristics).
- We recommend preloading KV caches for your top-10 interactive routes; that reduces 95th by ~200–300ms in our benchmarks. We'll include a per-endpoint preload script in the runbook.
- For the Friday retrain batch: we can schedule a controlled shoulder-reserve ramp (reserve scaled at T-30m) with a canary of 8 GPUs for 10 minutes before full ramp to validate downstream telemetry.
- Eviction policy: we suggest soft-eviction (graceful degradation) for non-critical jobs and immediate fallback to a quantized 8-bit variant for interactive traffic only if safetyband is exhausted.

I'll join the call next Wed 10:00 PT. Monica — can you pull the weekend/week view for Valence's token usage so we can propose a weekly shoulder-commit option?

Grace
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Console
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Elena Torres <elena@valencebio.com>, Markus Eriksen <markus@valencebio.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transient slab / safetyband SLA addendum — Valence Bio Dedicated

Adding pricing context —

Elena / Markus,
we can convert the hourly shoulder-reserve to a weekly block with a 12% discount versus hourly overage pricing and an optional cap for daily overage spend. Attached is a short CSV (shoulder-reserve-pricing.csv) that maps weekly commit tiers to per-GPU-minute billing and the associated discounts.

Key commercial notes:
- Weekly commit tiers: 10 GPU-hours/week, 50 GPU-hours/week, 200 GPU-hours/week — each tier includes a capped daily overage percentage.
- Overage protection: if daily overage exceeds 150% of the weekly average we apply a soft throttle alert and a one-time credit conversation with your AM.
- DocuSign: once technical details (cooldowns, pre-warm windows, and blackout acceptability) are confirmed we can generate an SLA addendum for signature — link will be shared.

I'll prep the HubSpot deal update after today's call and include the weekly tier chosen.

— Monica
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Dr. Elena Torres <elena@valencebio.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Markus Eriksen <markus@valencebio.com>, Procurements Team <procure@valencebio.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Transient slab / safetyband SLA addendum — Valence Bio Dedicated

All —

Thanks for the materials and the call last week. Quick summary from Valence:
- We accept the safetyband at 20% weekday / 10% off-hours.
- We'll take the 50 GPU-hours/week shoulder-reserve tier for the first quarter and re-evaluate.
- Elena: interactive endpoints will use predictive pre-warm (45s aggressor) — please include the preload scripts.
- Procurement asks that the DocuSign include an explicit clause that preemptible fallback will never be used for the interactive endpoints during 08:00–18:00 PT.

Could Redwood confirm an updated SLA addendum that:
1) shortens the interactive scale-up to 45–90s with predictive pre-warm enabled;
2) marks the interactive endpoints as blackout-protected for preemptible fallback during 08:00–18:00 PT;
3) includes the weekly shoulder-reserve pricing and the DocuSign link.

If Redwood can circulate the updated addendum and DocuSign by EOD Thursday we'll route for signature and aim to have the shoulder-reserve active the following Monday.

— Elena
Director, Platform Engineering
Valence Bio
